BUILD: Production-grade Size Charts pages for the Size Chart & Recommender Shopify app.

You need to build TWO files:
1. **List page**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.tsx` (EDIT existing)
2. **Editor page**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.$id.tsx` (CREATE new)

## CONTEXT
- Shopify embedded app, React Router 7 (NOT Remix), Polaris web components (`<s-*>`), TypeScript strict
- Prisma models: SizeChart (id, shop, name, type, category, data JSON, isDefault, status, createdAt, updatedAt), ChartAssignment (id, shop, sizeChartId, assignmentType, assignmentValue), SizeChartTemplate
- Templates defined in `app/lib/templates.ts` — `SIZE_CHART_TEMPLATES` array, `getCategories()`
- Plans defined in `app/lib/plans.ts` — `getPlan()`, `canCreateChart()`, `hasFeature()`
- Auth: `authenticate` from `../shopify.server`, `db` from `../db.server`
- Chart data JSON structure: `{ headers: string[], units: { default: string, available: string[] }, rows: Record<string, string>[] }`

## IMPORTANT RULES
1. Use Polaris web components ONLY: `<s-page>`, `<s-section>`, `<s-button>`, `<s-stack>`, `<s-box>`, `<s-text>`, `<s-heading>`, `<s-paragraph>`, `<s-badge>`, `<s-banner>`, `<s-link>`, `<s-divider>`, `<s-tabs>`, `<s-tab>`, `<s-empty-state>`, `<s-text-field>`, `<s-select>`, `<s-checkbox>`
2. `authenticate.admin(request)` at TOP of every loader/action
3. Every DB query: `where: { shop: session.shop }` — never leak cross-shop data
4. TypeScript strict — zero `any` types
5. Use `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()`, `useFetcher<typeof action>()`
6. `useAppBridge()` from `@shopify/app-bridge-react` for toasts
7. React Router 7 imports from `react-router` (NOT `@remix-run/*`)

## FILE 1: app.size-charts.tsx (List Page)

### Loader
Keep existing loader logic. It already loads charts with assignments, subscription, plan, templates.

### Action  
Keep existing action with intents: create-from-template, create-blank, delete, duplicate, toggle-status.

### Component — Complete Redesign:

**Page Header:**
- Title: "Size Charts"
- Primary action: "Create chart" button
- Subtitle showing chart count and plan limit

**Filter/Search Bar:**
- Category filter (All, Tops, Bottoms, Dresses, Shoes, Kids, Rings, Sportswear, General)
- Status filter (All, Active, Draft)
- Client-side filtering with useState

**Charts List:**
Each chart card should show:
- Chart name (bold, clickable link to editor `/app/size-charts/${chart.id}`)
- Category badge (e.g., "tops" → badge)
- Status badge: Active = `<s-badge tone="success">Active</s-badge>`, Draft = `<s-badge>Draft</s-badge>`
- Assignment count: "3 products assigned" or "No assignments"
- Last updated date
- Action buttons row: Edit, Publish/Unpublish, Duplicate, Delete (critical tone)

**Empty State (no charts):**
Compelling empty state with heading, description about reducing returns, and "Create your first chart" CTA.

**Template Picker (when creating):**
Show as a collapsible section or modal-like area:
- Grid of template cards grouped by category
- Each shows: template name, category, gender, row count
- "Use Template" button on each
- "Blank Chart" option at the end
- Close button to dismiss

**Sidebar:**
- Chart Limits: usage bar, plan name, upgrade CTA
- Quick Tips: helpful bullet points

### Code Quality
- Loading states on all buttons
- Toast feedback on all actions
- Proper error handling
- Client-side filter state

## FILE 2: app.size-charts.$id.tsx (Chart Editor — CREATE NEW)

This is the CORE feature — the size chart table editor.

### Loader
```typescript
export const loader = async ({ request, params }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {
  const { session } = await authenticate.admin(request);
  const shop = session.shop;
  const { id } = params;
  
  // Handle "new" as a special case for creating
  if (id === "new") {
    return { chart: null, assignments: [], isNew: true };
  }
  
  const chart = await db.sizeChart.findFirst({
    where: { id, shop },
    include: { assignments: true },
  });
  
  if (!chart) throw new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
  return { chart, assignments: chart.assignments, isNew: false };
};
```

### Action
Handle intents:
- `save` — Update chart name, category, status, data (the table JSON)
- `add-row` — Add empty row to chart data
- `remove-row` — Remove row by index
- `add-column` — Add column to headers and all rows
- `remove-column` — Remove column by header name
- `update-cell` — Update a single cell value (for inline editing)
- `save-assignments` — Update chart assignments
- `delete` — Delete chart and redirect to list

### Component — Full Table Editor:

**Page Header:**
- Back button to /app/size-charts
- Title: chart name (editable)
- Primary action: "Save" button
- Secondary: Status badge, "Publish"/"Unpublish" toggle

**Chart Details Section:**
- Name field (text input)
- Category selector (dropdown)
- Status indicator

**Table Editor Section (THE MAIN FEATURE):**
Build a full interactive table editor:
- Headers row (editable column names)
- Data rows with editable cells
- Each cell is an input field
- "Add Row" button at bottom
- "Add Column" button at right
- "Remove Row" button (X) on each row
- "Remove Column" button (X) on each column header
- Unit toggle (in/cm) at the top

Use `useState` to manage the table data locally, then submit it all on Save.

The table state should be:
```typescript
interface ChartData {
  headers: string[];
  units: { default: string; available: string[] };
  rows: Record<string, string>[];
}
```

**Table UI Implementation:**
Use HTML `<table>` with Polaris-styled cells (this is data display, not layout — tables are appropriate here):
```
| Size | Chest | Waist | Hips | [+ Col] |
|------|-------|-------|------|---------|
| S    | 34-36 | 28-30 | 34-36| [x]    |
| M    | 38-40 | 32-34 | 38-40| [x]    |
| [+ Add Row]                           |
```

Style the table with inline styles that match Polaris design (clean borders, proper padding, hover states).

**Product Assignment Section:**
- Show current assignments
- Assignment type selector: Product, Collection, Tag, Product Type, All Products
- Input for assignment value
- Add/Remove assignment buttons
- Note: For now, manual text entry for assignment values. Product picker can come later.

**Preview Section (Sidebar):**
- Live preview of how the size chart table will look
- Rendered as a clean read-only table
- Shows active unit system

**Sidebar — Chart Info:**
- Created date
- Last updated date
- Status
- Assignment count

### Styling for Table Editor
Use inline styles that match Shopify Polaris design language:
- Light borders (#e1e3e5)
- White background, subtle hover (#f6f6f7)
- Polaris text sizing
- Consistent padding (12px)
- Input fields that blend into cells

### CRITICAL: Save Flow
The save button should submit ALL chart data at once:
1. Collect chart name, category from form fields
2. Collect table data (headers + rows) from local state
3. Submit as JSON string in a hidden field
4. Action parses and saves to DB

### Navigation
- Back button links to `/app/size-charts`
- After delete, redirect to `/app/size-charts`
- Toast on save success/failure

### 1. `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.tsx` (edited)

- **Chart cards** — each card now shows: clickable chart name, Active/Draft badge (`tone="success"` vs. unstyled), category badge (`tone="info"`), assignment count or "No assignments", last-updated date, and four action buttons (Edit, Publish/Unpublish, Duplicate, Delete). The info region is wrapped in a `<div style={{ flex: 1 }}>` to push the action buttons to the right.
- **Usage bar** — the aside now shows a filled progress bar tracking published chart count against the plan limit, turning red when at the cap.
- **Warning banner** — shown at the top when the chart limit is reached, with a link to `/app/pricing`.

### 2. `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.$id.tsx` (created)

**Loader** — handles `id === "new"` (returns nulls for isNew flow), otherwise fetches `SizeChart` scoped to `session.shop` with assignments included. Dates are serialized to ISO strings. Throws 404 Response if not found.

**Action intents:**
- `save` — validates name, parses chart JSON, creates (and redirects) or updates the chart.
- `toggle-status` — flips active/draft, returns `newStatus` so the component can update local state without a full reload.
- `add-assignment` — upserts a `ChartAssignment` record; `assignmentType === "all"` uses value `"*"`.
- `remove-assignment` — `deleteMany` scoped to `shop`.
- `delete` — `deleteMany` scoped to `shop`, then redirects to `/app/size-charts`.

**`TableEditor` component** — fully interactive inline table editor:
- Editable column name inputs in the `<thead>` — renaming a header renames the key in every row.
- Remove-column button (×) per header; disabled when only one column remains.
- Add-column (+) button in the header's extra cell.
- Editable cell inputs in `<tbody>` rows.
- Remove-row button (×) per row.
- "Add row" button in a footer `<tr>` spanning all columns.
- Unit toggle buttons (in/cm etc.) above the table, styled to indicate the active unit.
- Alternating row background for readability.

**`ChartPreview` component** — read-only table rendered in the `slot="aside"`, updates live as the editor state changes. Shows active unit system and row count in a footer strip.

**Save flow** — `handleSave` serializes the full `ChartData` state to JSON and submits via `fetcher.submit`. For `id === "new"`, the action creates the record and issues a `redirect` to `/app/size-charts/<new-id>?saved=1`; the component clears the `?saved=1` param on mount and shows a toast.

**Product Assignments section** — lists current assignments with type badge and value; each has a "Remove" button. The add form has a type `<select>` and a conditional value `<input>` (hidden when type is "all"), with Enter-key support. Only rendered when the chart is not new; a banner prompts saving first otherwise.

**Sidebar — Chart Info** — shows created/updated timestamps, assignment count, and row count.

**Sidebar — Danger Zone** — Delete button that submits the `delete` intent, followed by explanatory text.

7. Test Duplicate and Delete from the list page.
